summary: The Federal Correctional Officer Paycheck Protection Act of 2026 aims to improve recruitment and retention of Federal correctional officers by increasing their base rates of pay by 35 percent. The bill applies to certain employees of the Bureau of Prisons whose duties relate to the custody, control, or supervision of inmates or who have routine direct inmate contact. It also includes certain prevailing rate employees up to grade 9 of the Federal Wage System. The pay increases are subject to a 5-year sunset period unless the Department of Justice Inspector General determines that the Bureau of Prisons has made measurable progress in eliminating augmentation and reducing excessive mandatory overtime.

affected_groups.effect: Receive a 35 percent increase to their base rate of pay, provided their duties relate to inmate custody, control, supervision, or routine direct contact.

Receive a 35 percent increase to their wage rates if classified at grade 9 or lower of the Federal Wage System and performing duties related to inmate custody, control, supervision, or direct contact.
affected_groups.group: Certain prevailing rate employees of the Bureau of Prisons

affected_groups.effect: Must conduct a review and submit a report to Congress evaluating the impacts on recruitment, retention, institutional safety, augmentation, and mandatory overtime.

key_provisions: Establishes a special base rate of pay for Federal correctional officers employed by the Bureau of Prisons, calculated by increasing the applicable General Schedule base rate or law enforcement officer special base rate by 35 percent, capped at level V of the Executive Schedule.

Requires the Attorney General to increase the wage rates of covered prevailing rate employees employed by the Bureau of Prisons and classified at grade 9 or lower of the Federal Wage System by 35 percent, capped at level IV of the Executive Schedule.
Provides that the new special base rates and increased wage rates count as basic pay for retirement, life insurance, and other applicable purposes.
Sets a 5-year sunset date on the pay authorities granted by the act.
Requires the Inspector General of the Department of Justice to conduct a review and report to Congress not later than 180 days before the 5-year expiration.

Allows the pay authorities to continue past 5 years if the Inspector General determines the Bureau of Prisons has demonstrated measurable progress in eliminating non-custodial employee augmentation and reducing excessive mandatory overtime.
missing_information: The total financial cost of the pay increases.
The exact number of employees who would qualify for the 35 percent pay increase.
